components.html:
Zaak data in a form

Every row shows one property of the zaak: on the left the expression, next to it what it renders. ZAC puts the zaak in the form's template context, so zaak.identificatie in a content component is all that is needed — there is no ZAC attribute or property involved. Nested properties work as you would expect: zaak.zaaktype.omschrijving.

Three helper functions come with it: ZAC_opmaakDatum(zaak.startdatum) and ZAC_opmaakBoolean(zaak.isOpen) for display, which takes two labels of its own — ZAC_opmaakBoolean(zaak.isOpgeschort, "Opgeschort", "Loopt") — and falls back to Ja and Nee, and ZAC_opmaakLijst to read one property of every element of a list. Several values can go in one sentence, which is what a content component is for.

Almost nothing reports a mistake. A misspelled property renders as empty, and so does a property read through an object the zaak does not have — zaak.behandelaar.naam on an unassigned zaak is a correct expression, not a mistake, and renders nothing rather than failing. An object renders [object Object]. Only an unknown function is loud, and only in the browser console. The last panel shows each of those. Markup in a zaak value is removed before the form ever sees it, so a value cannot inject anything.

Every other row is wrapped in ZAC_opmaakLegeWaarde, so both behaviours are on screen at once: without it an empty property renders as nothing, with it as a dash. It is the same empty pipe the rest of ZAC uses, so a dash here means the same as a dash in the zaak screen.
